items.title: DeepSeek shipped a faster multimodal Flash model
items.oneliner: DeepSeek's V4.1 Flash 1017 cuts KV cache to one quarter and claims stronger coding, reasoning, and vision at lower cost.

items.title: Black Forest Labs shrank image generation to laptops
items.oneliner: FLUX 3 Image Klein packs 5.6B parameters, 4K editing, and 4 second renders onto consumer GPUs.

items.title: Ultramarine is pushing enterprise AI pricing down
items.oneliner: Ultramarine 1 Flash claims $0.13 per task and 6.5% fewer tokens, turning efficiency into a direct pricing weapon.

items.title: Claude found better quantum circuits
items.oneliner: Anthropic says Claude beat published quantum circuit designs, which matters because algorithmic gains can arrive before better hardware.

items.title: Ad tech was used to deliver spyware
items.oneliner: Citizen Lab says mercenary spyware rode ad-tech pipes, a reminder that your ad stack can become an exploit chain.

items.title: Claude solved a long-running crypto mystery
items.oneliner: Claude traced NIST ECDSA curve seeds to lrand48 and Unix timestamps, closing a decades-old trust question in public cryptography.

items.title: MapQuest exposed neighborhood surveillance camera locations
items.oneliner: MapQuest now maps Flock and other street cameras, making local surveillance infrastructure visible instead of quietly ambient.

items.title: PyTorch got a much leaner memory planner
items.oneliner: A new PyTorch knapsack solver cuts peak RAM by up to 20x, which directly expands what fits on existing hardware.

items.title: ESP32 firmware now runs in the browser
items.oneliner: Esp32sim emulates real ESP32 firmware in-browser, which could collapse embedded debugging and demo loops from hours to minutes.

items.title: AI benchmarks still miss most real work
items.oneliner: Mercor says 90% of US working hours map poorly to AI benchmarks, so leaderboard wins still overstate business readiness.
